exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Finding the Way in the Park
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Jake
transcript.text: Excuse me, do you happen to know where the fountain is?

transcript.speaker: Linlin
transcript.text: Yes. It's on the north side of the park, about two hundred metres from here.

transcript.speaker: Jake
transcript.text: Great. How do I get there?

transcript.speaker: Linlin
transcript.text: Follow the main path along the river until you see a small bridge.

transcript.speaker: Jake
transcript.text: And then?

transcript.speaker: Linlin
transcript.text: When you see the bridge, you are close to the fountain. It's just behind it.

transcript.speaker: Jake
transcript.text: Is the boat lake far from there?

transcript.speaker: Linlin
transcript.text: No, it's nearby. You can rent a pedal boat right next to the fountain.

exercises.translation_cn: Jake 问喷泉在哪;玲玲说在公园北侧、离这约两百米;让他沿河边主路走到一座小桥;看到桥就快到喷泉了,喷泉在桥后面;划船的湖就在附近,喷泉旁边可以租脚踏船。

questions.stem: Where is the fountain?
options: On the north side of the park.
On the south side of the lake.

questions.stem: How far is the fountain from where they stand?
What should Jake follow to get there?
options: The main path along the river.

questions.stem: How will Jake know he is close to the fountain?
options: He will see a small bridge.
He will reach the car park.

questions.stem: What can Jake do near the fountain?

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 A Park with No Roads
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: In the far north of Sweden lies a vast park with no roads and no towns.
Long ago, sheets of ice covered its mountains, leaving behind many glaciers.
The Sami people made this remote land their home and lived by following reindeer.
In 1909 the area became a national park to keep it in its natural state.
Today no one but the Sami may live inside its boundaries.
exercises.translation_cn: 瑞典最北部有一座没有道路和城镇的辽阔公园;很久以前冰雪覆盖群山,留下许多冰川;萨米人以这片偏远土地为家,靠跟随驯鹿生活;1909年此地成为国家公园以保持其自然状态;如今除萨米人外无人可在其边界内居住。

questions.stem: Where is this park?
options: In the far north of Sweden.

questions.stem: What did the ice leave behind when it melted?
How did the Sami people live?
Why did the area become a national park in 1909?
options: To keep it in its natural state.

questions.stem: Who may live inside the park today?

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Planning a Trip to the Theme Park
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Yuhui
transcript.text: Let's plan our day at the theme park tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Good idea. I really want to try the roller coaster first.

transcript.speaker: Yuhui
transcript.text: Sure, but the morning queues are long. Let's do the water rides first.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: All right. And I'd love to see the dolphin show too.

transcript.speaker: Yuhui
transcript.text: The show starts at two o'clock, so let's have lunch before that.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Where can we eat? I'm not sure the restaurants are open early.

transcript.speaker: Yuhui
transcript.text: Don't worry. There are plenty of restaurants near the lake.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Perfect. Then we'll watch the fireworks display at night before we leave.

exercises.translation_cn: 宇辉和 Ben 计划明天去主题公园;Ben 想先玩过山车;宇辉说早上排队长,先玩水上项目;Ben 还想看海豚表演;表演两点开始,先吃午饭;Ben 担心餐厅没开;宇辉说湖边有很多餐厅;最后晚上看烟花再离开。

questions.stem: What does Ben want to try first?
Why does Yuhui suggest the water rides first?
options: They are cheaper in the morning.
The roller coaster queues are long.

questions.stem: When does the dolphin show start?
Where can they have lunch?
What will they do before leaving at night?

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 The Green Lungs of the City
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Our city's wetland park is a green, watery world full of life.
Trees and bushes grow along the banks, and birds nest among them.
When it was planned, the designers tried hard to limit the impact of people.
All the new buildings were made in a traditional way to fit into nature.
Because it cleans water and makes oxygen, people call it the green lungs of the city.
exercises.translation_cn: 我们城市的湿地公园是一个充满生命、绿意盎然的水世界;岸边长着树木和灌木,鸟儿在其中筑巢;规划时设计者尽力减少人为影响;所有新建筑都以传统方式建造以融入自然;因为它净化水、产生氧气,人们称它为城市的绿肺。

questions.stem: What kind of place is the wetland park?
options: A green, watery world full of life.

questions.stem: What grows along the banks?
What did the designers try hard to do?
options: Build as many shops as possible.

questions.stem: How were the new buildings made?
options: In a traditional way to fit into nature.

questions.stem: Why is it called the 'green lungs' of the city?
options: Because it is shaped like lungs.
Because it cleans water and makes oxygen.
Because only green things are sold there.

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Asking for Directions
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Tourist
transcript.text: Pardon me, how do I get to the underwater corridor?

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: Go straight ahead until you come to the big aquarium.

transcript.speaker: Tourist
transcript.text: Is it far from here?

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: No, it's about a hundred metres on your left.

transcript.speaker: Tourist
transcript.text: Can I see the polar bears on the way?

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: Yes. When you pass the dolphin pool, the polar bears are just beyond it.

transcript.speaker: Tourist
transcript.text: Thank you. And where are the restaurants?

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: They're on the east side, so you can eat while watching the fish swim by.

exercises.translation_cn: 游客问怎么去水下走廊;向导让他一直往前走到大水族馆;离这约一百米、在左边;路上能看到北极熊;经过海豚池后,北极熊就在那后面;餐厅在东侧,可以边吃边看鱼游过。

questions.stem: Where does the tourist want to go?
How far is it from where they stand?
What can the tourist see on the way?
Where are the polar bears?
Why are the restaurants a good place to eat?
options: They are the cheapest in town.
You can eat while watching the fish.
They are next to the car park.

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 Tips for Visiting a Park
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here are a few simple tips for visiting a national park.
First, follow the marked routes and do not wander off on your own.
Second, remember that hunting and picking flowers are usually prohibited.
Third, carry your own water and food, since shops may be far away.
If everyone protects the park, its rare animals and plants can live in peace.
exercises.translation_cn: 这里有几条逛国家公园的简单贴士:第一,沿标好的路线走,别自己乱跑;第二,记住狩猎和采花通常是被禁止的;第三,自带水和食物,因为商店可能很远;如果人人都保护公园,园里珍稀的动植物就能安然生活。

questions.stem: What are these tips for?
What does the first tip say?
What is usually prohibited in the park?
Why should visitors carry their own food and water?
options: Because the park sells nothing fresh.
Because shops may be far away.

questions.stem: What happens if everyone protects the park?
options: Its rare animals and plants can live in peace.
